question: Why did the error rate go up on 10 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: Upstream identity-db service is experiencing degraded performance, causing auth service errors.
why_chain: The error rate in auth service increased due to upstream identity-db service returning HTTP 503 errors.
The identity-db service is the upstream dependency of the auth service, and its degraded performance is causing the auth service to fail.
The identity-db service is experiencing degraded performance, as evidenced by the status page stating it is investigating degraded performance.

contributing_factors.description: The auth service is experiencing increased latency due to upstream identity-db service.
why_chain: The p95 latency for auth service increased due to upstream identity-db service returning HTTP 503 errors.
The increased latency is a result of the upstream identity-db service failing to respond within the expected time frame.
The identity-db service is the upstream dependency of the auth service, and its failure is causing the auth service to experience increased latency.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a configuration change in the auth service.
ruled_out.reason: The error rate increase is concentrated in the auth service, and the change point is at the same time as the error rate increase.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a change in the traffic to the auth service.
ruled_out.reason: The request volume for the auth service did not change significantly, and the error rate increase is not explained by a change in traffic.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a change in the infrastructure of the auth service.
ruled_out.reason: The infrastructure of the auth service did not change, and the error rate increase is not explained by a change in infrastructure.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a change in the data input to the auth service.
ruled_out.reason: The data input to the auth service did not change, and the error rate increase is not explained by a change in data.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service auth rose from 0.40% to 5.00% (+1146%), with a change point at 2026-03-10T09:30:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service auth: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.12).
At the same time, request volume for service auth stayed about the same (1080 per 5 min before, 1341 per 5 min after, +24%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service auth rose (90 ms before, 164 ms after, +81%).
Upstream identity-db returning HTTP 503 for auth (auth; 2 min after the change; record R008)
auth: ERROR upstream identity-db timeout after 3 retries (auth, ap-south; 5 min after the change; record R009)
auth: ERROR upstream identity-db timeout after 3 retries (auth, eu-west; 17 min after the change; record R010)
auth: ERROR upstream identity-db timeout after 3 retries (auth, us-east; 17 min after the change; record R011)
identity-db status page: investigating degraded performance (auth; 30 min after the change; record R012)

reasons: ✓ A change event (alerts) lines up in time (2 min after the change).
✓ 4 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Contact the identity-db service team to investigate the degraded performance and provide a fix.
Monitor the identity-db service closely and take immediate action if it degrades again.
Review and optimize the retry logic in the auth service to reduce the impact of upstream failures.
